name: MACAAL
funding: Fondation Alliances, set up in 2009 by Othman Lazraq, funds it. The Lazraq family runs the listed property developer Alliances. No other funder is named.

name: Musée Yves Saint Laurent Marrakech
funding: Opened 2017, paid for by Pierre Bergé's 2015 sale of Moroccan art and run on Jardin Majorelle ticket income (700k+ visitors a year); a luxury-fashion legacy.

name: L'Appartement 22
funding: Founded by curator Abdellah Karroum. Supported through non-commercial international research grants, Prince Claus Fund, and independent publishing sales.

name: Le Cube – independent art room
funding: Small artist-run space founded 2005 by Elisabeth Piskernik; residencies paid by artists, partners are foreign cultural institutes and embassies.

name: Musée Mohammed VI d'Art Moderne et Contemporain (MMVI)
funding: State museum run since 2014 by the Fondation Nationale des Musées, built with Ministry of Culture and Fonds Hassan II money; partners include Royal Air Maroc.

name: Contemporary Art Museum of the Kasbah
funding: Run by the National Foundation of Museums. Restoration and design cost 13 million dirhams; the Wilaya of Tangier supervised it, with the Ministry of Culture, APDN and the Foundation contributing.

name: Associação Núcleo de Arte
funding: Artists' association with over 100 members. State funding ended in the civil war; a late-1990s profile names Hivos as donor. No current funder list is published.

name: Fundação Fernando Leite Couto
funding: Sponsors in 2025: Moza Banco, Nedbank, Standard Bank and the Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation. Prize partners include Óbidos council, the Portugal-Mozambique Chamber of Commerce and Camões.

name: Franco-Namibian Cultural Centre (FNCC)
funding: Binational centre under Namibian law, funded by the French government. Namibia gave the land and France paid for the building; foundation stone laid in 1998.

name: National Art Gallery of Namibia
funding: State-owned art gallery. Bank Windhoek partners on its 2025/2026 Triennial.

name: Kathmandu Triennale
funding: Siddhartha Arts Foundation with Nepal Academy of Fine Arts (2026); 2022 edition backed by embassies, Saraf Foundation, Gorkha Brewery, Himalayan Bank, Toyota.
